title: Passive quantum memory
why: Gemini 4 Argon does most of the proof work for Stanford physicist Patrick Hayden's claim that a three-dimensional quantum system can protect stored information on its own, against both heat and small disturbances, a central open question since Alexei Kitaev's work on quantum computing.

title: Diffie–Hellman problem
why: Working with Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Opus 5.5, Yuwen Zhou removes a condition that Ueli Maurer's 30-year-old result needed, showing that cracking Diffie–Hellman key exchange is as hard as the discrete logarithm problem once a short hint is given.

title: Non-overlapping codes
why: Simon Blackburn proves the best possible limit on how large a non-overlapping code can be, improving Vladimir Levenshtein's 1970 bound, with GPT-6 Astra writing one of the paper's key proofs.

title: Frostbite
why: Architect Labs' AI agents design a new kind of CPU on their own, from its instruction set to the final chip layout, and in simulation it does 4.59 times as much work per watt as a modern in-order core; no chip has been made yet.

title: Smoktunowicz's gap theorem
why: Working alone for 94 minutes, GPT-6.2 Astra writes the first known computer-checked proof of a 2006 theorem by Agata Smoktunowicz about how fast certain algebras can grow, by a route of its own rather than the published one, Vals AI reports.

title: El-Zahar–Erdős conjecture
why: Chenghua Liu and Boning Meng, working with GPT-6, disprove a 1985 question of Mohamed El-Zahar and Paul Erdős by building graphs that need many colors yet never split into two separate, unconnected parts that each need many colors.

title: Stafford's conjecture
why: AI agents write the first complete proof of a 1978 conjecture of Toby Stafford about Weyl algebras, and check all of it in Lean, for Christopher Albert, Johanna Moser and Maximilian Philipp.

title: McKay–Praeger conjecture
why: Ning Su and Binzhou Xia, working with GPT-6, prove that almost every graph in which all points look alike is built from a group, as Brendan McKay and Cheryl Praeger conjectured.

title: Sample compression
why: Google's Cogentic agents running Gemini 4 Carbon prove on their own that any learning problem can be summed up by a number of examples roughly the square of its complexity, the first such bound for a conjecture Sally Floyd and Manfred Warmuth posed in 1995.

title: Additive squares
why: GPT-6 writes almost all of a paper for Jeffrey Shallit that builds an endless string of six numbers in which no two neighboring blocks have the same length and the same sum, solving a problem open for more than 50 years, and checks it in Lean.

title: Bounded integer programming
why: Given two earlier papers by Lin Chen, Yuchen Mao and Guochuan Zhang, GPT-6 finds a faster algorithm than theirs for a basic kind of optimization problem, with almost no human input.

title: QMA and QCMA
why: With GPT-6 Astra producing nearly the entire proof, Yiming Wang shows a setting in which quantum proofs can convince a verifier of things that no stack of classical proofs can.

title: Cubic Schrödinger equation
why: Xi Chen, working with ChatGPT 6, builds waves on a square torus whose energy keeps spreading to finer and finer scales without limit, answering a question of Jean Bourgain.

title: nginx2root
why: With no human guidance, Xint's AI platform finds four flaws that let attackers run code remotely in nginx, the web server behind about a third of the web; a Xint researcher found a fifth, hidden since 2015.

title: GPU chip design
why: OpenAI's models rewrite parts of AMD's flagship GPU design for up to 14% better power, performance and area, about a year of progress in under five months, and AMD puts some of the changes in a chip it sent for manufacturing.

title: Topological overlap
why: GPT-6 Astra finds the proof, following Sergey Norin's directions, that settles exactly how crowded any drawing of a high-dimensional simplex must get at some point, confirming a conjecture of Boris Bukh, Jiří Matoušek and Gabriel Nivasch.

title: Shortest paths on 4-polytopes
why: Igor Pak, working extensively with ChatGPT, proves that finding the shortest path across the surface of a four-dimensional convex shape is computationally hard, disproving several conjectures along the way.

title: Positroid conjecture
why: ChatGPT-6 Astra writes a 117-page first proof of the positroid conjecture of Luis Ferroni, Katharina Jochemko and Benjamin Schröter, with Ferroni only steering; GPT-6.2 Astra then simplifies it and Claude Opus 5.5 checks it.

title: Navier–Stokes blowup
why: Working with Claude, Tristan Buckmaster and Levent Alpöge post a proof that the equations of fluid flow can break down even with no force pushing the fluid, the version of the Millennium Prize problem experts wanted; a data file the proof depends on isn't out yet.

title: Euler blowup
why: With AI help, Levent Alpöge, Tristan Buckmaster and Matei Coiculescu prove that an ideal fluid in a box whose sides wrap around can start spinning infinitely fast at a point in finite time, with every step checked in Lean.

title: McEliece challenges
why: MiniMax's unreleased internal model recovers the secret keys to 55 unsolved McEliece code-breaking challenges and makes the first practical breaks of several retired candidates for US encryption standards, MiniMax says.

title: Metal–organic frameworks
why: MOFGen, a team of AI agents built by Théo Jaffrelot Inizan, Kristin Persson and Omar Yaghi, designs new metal–organic frameworks, porous crystals that can capture carbon dioxide and pull water from air, and chemists make four of them in the lab.

title: MONAI Label zero-day
why: AI agents run by suspected China-linked hackers through the Cairn framework find an unknown flaw in MONAI Label, a medical imaging server, and use it to take full control of a university server, Amazon Threat Intelligence reports.

title: Masullo's GRH proof
why: Within hours of Ravi Vakil posting Alessandro Masullo's proposed proof of the generalized Riemann hypothesis, written without AI, several mathematicians report problems in it that they found with AI models.

title: Valiant's conjecture
why: An internal Claude model proves the algebraic version of P versus NP that Leslie Valiant posed in 1979, showing that the permanent of a matrix can't be computed efficiently with addition and multiplication alone; Lean accepts the 70-page proof, but no mathematician has checked it yet.
